items.title: DoorDash Reaches $131M Settlement With NYC Regarding Underpaid Delivery Workers: ‘We Screwed Up’
items.summary: DoorDash is owning its mistakes with New York City delivery workers. On Tuesday, September 22, the company posted a news release on its website saying it reached a $131.5 million settlement with New York City’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) over compliance with pay rules for its delivery workers. items.title: ‘We Screwed Up’: DoorDash Stock Rises After Admitting It Underpaid Delivery Workers
items.summary: Food delivery service  DoorDash  has settled a dispute with New York City over claims it underpaid its tipped workers.  More than 200,000 Dashers, as the firm’s delivery workers are called, will receive the payments.  “After years of corporate greed and impunity, we are holding DoorDash to account,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said of the settlement, which he called  “a major victory for the working people who call New York City home.”

items.title: DoorDash to Pay $131.5 Million to Resolve NYC Investigation Into Minimum-Pay Law Compliance
items.summary: The bulk of the settlement concerns the law’s requirement that drivers are paid for time spent on the app between deliveries, known as “on-call time.”

items.title: DoorDash reaches $131.5M settlement with NYC over courier pay
items.summary: The delivery company will pay $12.3 million to more than 200,000 couriers who were underpaid or paid late under the city’s 2023 wage rules.
